clusters.name: Virgo Cluster

centre.note: the mean direction of the members drawn

depth.note: the published rms scatter of the cluster's SBF distances

clusters.catalogue: The Extended Virgo Cluster Catalog (Kim and others 2014, ApJS 215, 22; VizieR J/ApJS/215/22), members by the infall model; distances of 84 of them from Mei and others 2007, ApJ 655, 144 (VizieR J/ApJ/655/144)
clusters.source: Mei and others 2007, ApJ 655, 144 (arXiv astro-ph/0702510): 'The remaining 79 galaxies have a narrow distribution around our adopted mean distance of 16.5+/-0.1 (random mean error) +/-1.1 Mpc (systematic). The rms distance scatter of this sample is 0.6+/-0.1 Mpc' (abstract, read 2026-10-20). Kim and others 2014, ApJS 215, 22 (VizieR, read 2026-10-20).

clusters.name: Coma Cluster

centre.note: the mean direction of the members drawn

depth.note: the members' spread on the sky, read as the same spread in depth (a cluster is round: an assumption)

clusters.catalogue: Spectroscopic redshift survey of the Coma cluster (Kang and others 2025, ApJS 278, 51; VizieR J/ApJS/278/51), the members its own flag names; sizes and colours from the Sloan Digital Sky Survey (DR17)
clusters.source: Kang and others 2025, ApJS 278, 51 (VizieR J/ApJS/278/51/table2, read 2026-10-20). SDSS DR17 photometry through SkyServer (https://skyserver.sdss.org/dr17, read 2026-10-20).

clusters.name: Fornax Cluster

centre.note: the mean direction of the members drawn

depth.note: the published rms scatter of the cluster's SBF distances

clusters.catalogue: Galaxies in the Fornax Cluster (Ferguson 1989, AJ 98, 367; VizieR VII/180), the likely members
clusters.source: Blakeslee and others 2009, ApJ 694, 556 (arXiv 0901.1138): 'The resulting Fornax distance modulus is 31.51 +/-0.03 +/-0.15 mag, 20.0 +/-0.3 +/-1.4 Mpc ... The rms distance scatter for the early-type Fornax galaxies is 0.49 Mpc' (abstract, read 2026-10-20). Ferguson 1989 (VizieR VII/180, read 2026-10-20).

clusters.name: Perseus Cluster

centre.note: the mean direction of the members drawn

depth.note: the members' spread on the sky, read as the same spread in depth (a cluster is round: an assumption)

clusters.source: Kang and others 2024, ApJS 272, 22 (VizieR J/ApJS/272/22/table2, read 2026-10-20). SDSS DR17 photometry through SkyServer (https://skyserver.sdss.org/dr17, read 2026-10-20).
